utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, good afternoon to you. Could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please take a seat. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Julian Nicholls with Joanna Korner and Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you all. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman with Milan Trbojevic, Barbara Baruch and Brian Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good afternoon to you. So before we bring in the witness and conclude, hopefully, there are two things I have received today, I barely had time to go through it, but there is another motion from -- forthcoming from the Prosecution for the application of a 92 bis -- Petrovac municipality. I suppose you have had it. To be frank with you, I haven't had time to go through the comparative study to see whether it is indeed -- whether it is indeed -- let me see. This is the one. Have you received it, Mr. Ackerman, by the way?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Ten or 15 minutes ago, Your Honour. I have not had a chance to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Me too. I mean, I only received it now. The submission of the Prosecution is that the evidence of this person is of a cumulative nature to the statements of two witnesses which are indicated and who the Prosecution tends to produce viva voce. As I told you, I haven't had time to go through the -- any statement of these other two persons, and I don't even know whether I have these statements of these other two persons to be true. I still have to check with my staff. Can I rely on you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You do, Your Honour, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's the important thing but I haven't had time, Ms. Korner, to consult with anyone. Can I rely on you, Mr. Ackerman, that within a week from today you will be in a position to give us feedback.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I believe that we will be able to file a response by the end of next week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fine with me. So with this partially confidential motion, we will deal with it as we go along, either next week or the week after, after we receive some kind of response from the Defence, Ms. Korner. Is that all right with you?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is. And finally, the solicitors have responded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was other thing I was coming to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in open session so I'll leave it at the moment simply to say this, we will respond on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I was just pointing that out to you and asking you for a response.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You are in no hurry but as soon as the response comes in we will deal with it with the utmost celerity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else before we proceed? Mr. Ackerman, Mr. Nicholls? Curtains, I'm so sad to see members of the public coming into the public gallery the moment I'm declaring the sitting to go into closed session and to disappoint them so much. Let's go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Only point, Your Honours, Ms. Korner asked me to convey her apologies that she had to leave early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are still not in open session. Yes, that brings to us an end for the time being. We will be resuming on the 14th of April as per the latest scheduling order that we have handed down. I take it, Mr. Ackerman, that you have received a list of the witnesses that will be brought over during that week and the week to follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you. So I take it that everyone will be prepared to go through those witnesses during those days. On our part, Mr. Ackerman, I am expressing the -- also the feelings of Judge Janu and Judge Taya, before you depart, we wish you a safe journey back home and also a quick recovery, and we look forward to having you back where you belong.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm very grateful for that and rest assured I will be back stronger than ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. So the trial stands adjourned until the 14th, no? 14th of April. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 4.16 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of April, 2003.
